title: Normalized finite scalar comparison of rational realizations
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E,F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $i:E\to F$ be a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra embedding, with arbitrary ramification. Let $X$ be noetherian and finite-dimensional, with $\ell$ invertible at every stalk, and use the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $s_E,s_F$ be rational module realization data [def-sf-rational-module-realization-datum], with normalized inclusions $\alpha_E:B_{E,X}\to E_X$, $\alpha_F:B_{F,X}\to F_X$ and functors $J_E,J_F$. Use sheaf modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The completed integral coefficient map $c:B_{E,X}\to B_{F,X}$ is the one whose quotient maps are induced by $i$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Its actual derived tensor, restricted to the bounded constructible complete integral category [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], is denoted $I_{F/E}$. Let $T_{F/E}$ be its raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], with the well-defined restriction and scalar-localization functor supplied by [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Write $\mu_{r,s}$ for the canonical derived balancing comparison for a composite of coefficient maps, normalized on K-flat representatives by $z\otimes(y\otimes x)\mapsto z\,s(y)\otimes x$, with inverse inserting $1$; it is the quotient-reduction normalization of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower].

Define a rational realization scalar comparison datum for $i,s_E,s_F$ to consist of a ring-sheaf map $\gamma:E_X\to F_X$ normalized on every section by $\gamma(b)(x)=i(b(x))$, the coefficient-square equality $c\,;\,\alpha_F=\alpha_E\,;\,\gamma$, and a natural isomorphism
$$\theta:T_{F/E}\,;\,J_F\xrightarrow{\sim}J_E\,;\,(F_X\otimes^L_{E_X}-).$$
For every integral $K$ require the following exact normalization. The route from $J_F(Q_F I_{F/E}K)$ through $\theta_{Q_EK}$, extension of the object equality $J_E(Q_EK)=E_X\otimes^L_{B_{E,X}}K$, and $\mu_{\alpha_E,\gamma}$ equals the route through the object equality $J_F(Q_F I_{F/E}K)=F_X\otimes^L_{B_{F,X}}I_{F/E}K$ and $\mu_{c,\alpha_F}$, with the common target identified by the coefficient-square equality. Thus both routes are the balanced identification through $F_X\otimes^L_{B_{E,X}}K$ using the actual integral extension. This is a record of the specified data and equation, not a theorem that the record is inhabited; no tower, pullback or pentagon assertion is imposed by this definition.
